newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police arrest two over fake U.S. dollars.
newsitem.headline: HK police arrest two over fake U.S. dollars.

text.p: Hong Kong police have arrested two men, one a foreign national, suspected of having circulated counterfeit U.S. banknotes in the territory, a senior police source said on Monday.
The suspects, whose names were not disclosed, were arrested last week in two separate cases, the source said.
"We've examined the notes, they're certainly counterfeit. That's the situation at the moment," the source told Reuters.
"Investigations are still going on. Two men have been arrested and been released on bail," he said.
One of the suspects is an ethnic Chinese Hong Kong resident, the other of another Asian nationality, he said. Police declined to give further details on the two cases.

Officers at a bank in the bustling Tsim Sha Tsui shopping area alerted police on April 1 after they became suspicious about more than a hundred US$100 notes that one of the suspects tried to deposit, a Chinese-language newspaper said.

Police experts later found more than 10 fake notes in the pile, the Ming Pao newspaper reported, adding that they were of superior quality and capable of eluding most fake currency detectors now used in Hong Kong banks.
The newspaper did not report on the other case.
The police source said he did not think the two cases were linked. "They are probably the same type of note but they are two different cases (that) we don't believe are linked."
